assembly_instructions: 1. Lay the two running rails at y=0, add evenly spaced cross ties, and use the rail heads as the datum for all wheel contact points.
2. Assemble the long welded locomotive main frame above the rails, then bolt on the front pilot beam, sloped pilot, front coupler, and rear drawbar pocket.

3. Build the three-axle leading truck under the smokebox, the four driving axles under the boiler barrel, and the three-axle trailing truck under the firebox; fit every port and starboard wheel to its named axle.
4. Add crank discs and crank pins to each driving wheel, then fit the port and starboard side rods across all four driving axles so torque from the geared axle is visibly distributed.
5. Mount the smokebox, boiler barrel, and split Belpaire firebox assembly: lower wrapper first, then shoulder sheets, crown sheet, throat sheet, and exposed backhead.
6. Fit the cab floor, cutaway cab shell, and cab roof behind the firebox while leaving the turbine train below the cab open to view.
7. Install the Westinghouse ahead turbine, smaller reverse turbine, reduction gearbox, driveshaft, oil cooler, and steam delivery pipe; connect the gearbox to the fourth driving axle housing.

8. Add boiler-top and side appliances: steam dome, Worthington feedwater heater, feedwater pump and pipe, paired air pumps, four separate exhaust stacks, bell, headlight, handrails, running boards, and smoke deflectors with stays and edge stiffeners.

9. Build the tender as a separate underframe with two four-axle trucks, all sixteen tender wheels, thin floor plate, open water cistern, internal baffles, coal bunker walls, slope sheet, exposed coal load, filler hatch, water outlet pipe, rear deck, ladder, tool box, and rear coupler.

10. Connect locomotive and tender with the drawbar and verify that every truck wheel rests on the rails, the tender contents remain visible from the ISO view, and the turbine-to-geared-axle power path remains unobstructed.

info.japanese_name: ペンシルバニア鉄道 S2形 蒸気タービン機関車 (1944)
info.english_name: Pennsylvania Railroad class S2 steam-turbine locomotive
info.summary: One-off 1944 experimental 6-8-6 direct-drive steam-turbine locomotive (PRR #6200). The only locomotive ever built with a 6-8-6 wheel arrangement.
info.description: The Pennsylvania Railroad's S2 (#6200) was a one-off experimental steam-turbine locomotive built by Baldwin in 1944 to see whether marine-style direct-drive turbines could keep steam competitive against emerging diesels. It is the only locomotive ever built with a 6-8-6 wheel arrangement — a three-axle leading truck, four driven axles (68-inch driving wheels), and a three-axle trailing truck under a massive Belpaire firebox. Rather than reciprocating pistons, the S2 used a Westinghouse ahead-turbine (with a smaller reverse turbine) geared through a reduction transmission to one driving axle; the remaining driving axles were connected via conventional side rods. The engine incorporated a Worthington feedwater heater, a quadruple exhaust stack to give the turbine enough draft, and distinctive 'elephant-ear' smoke deflectors (added December 1946 at Altoona) to lift the plume over the unusually long boiler. A 180-P-85 tender with sixteen wheels on two 4-axle trucks carried 19,500 US gal of water and 37.5 short tons of coal. The S2 ran passenger service in 1944–1949 but suffered from turbine blade wear and poor efficiency at low speeds, and was scrapped in 1952.
info.status: Retired / scrapped; Wikipedia docs CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.label: Scale used in scene
facts.value: 0.5× real dimensions; modeled length with tender about 18.7 m from pilot to tender rear.

facts.label: Wheel arrangement
facts.value: 6-8-6: three leading axles, four coupled driving axles, three trailing axles.

facts.label: Prototype length
facts.value: 122 ft 7¼ in (37.37 m) over locomotive and tender.

facts.label: Prototype height
facts.value: 16 ft (4.88 m), represented as about 2.44 m at 0.5× scale.

facts.label: Driving wheels
facts.value: 8 × 68 in (1.73 m) drivers; scene radius about 0.43 m at 0.5× scale.

facts.label: Leading and trailing wheels
facts.value: 36 in leading wheels and 42 in trailing wheels, modeled at about 0.23 m and 0.27 m radii at scale.

facts.label: Boiler pressure
facts.value: 310 psi (2.1 MPa), shown by the single large boiler barrel feeding turbine pipework.

facts.label: Turbine output
facts.value: About 6,900 hp peak and 6,000 hp rated through a Westinghouse direct-drive turbine and reduction gearing.

facts.label: Tender capacity
facts.value: 180-P-85 tender: 19,500 US gal water and 37.5 short tons coal on two 4-axle trucks.

facts.label: Signature details
facts.value: Four exhaust stacks, Worthington feedwater heater, elephant-ear smoke deflectors, Belpaire firebox shoulders, and visible turbine gearbox.

parts.name: Locomotive Main Frame
parts.role: Long welded locomotive bed frame carries the boiler, trucks, driving axles, turbine, and drawbar loads.

parts.name: Front Pilot Beam
parts.role: Heavy transverse beam at the nose supports the pilot and front coupler.

parts.name: Sloped Pilot / Cowcatcher
parts.role: Low wedge-shaped pilot clears track obstructions ahead of the leading truck.

parts.name: Front Knuckle Coupler
parts.role: Front coupler is the external pulling interface on the pilot beam.

parts.name: Cylindrical Smokebox
parts.role: Short front chamber collects combustion gas and turbine exhaust draft before discharge through the four stacks.

parts.name: Round Smokebox Door
parts.role: Circular front door gives maintenance access to the smokebox tube sheet.

parts.name: PRR 6200 Number Plate
parts.role: Small brass number plate identifies the one-off PRR 6200 prototype on the smokebox door.

parts.name: Centered Headlight
parts.role: Front-facing headlight is centered above the smokebox door for passenger-service visibility.

parts.name: Long Boiler Barrel
parts.role: Main 310 psi pressure vessel generates steam and visually defines the S2's very long nose.

parts.name: Belpaire Firebox Lower Wrapper
parts.role: Lower Belpaire firebox wrapper carries the grate space over the trailing truck without hiding the under-cab turbine.

parts.name: Port Belpaire Shoulder Sheet
parts.role: Port raised shoulder forms the square Belpaire upper corner instead of a plain rectangular firebox slab.

parts.name: Starboard Belpaire Shoulder Sheet
parts.role: Starboard raised shoulder mirrors the port Belpaire sheet and makes the squared firebox top readable.

parts.name: Flat Belpaire Crown Sheet
parts.role: Flat crown sheet caps the firebox and distinguishes the Belpaire wrapper from a round-top boiler.

parts.name: Belpaire Throat Sheet
parts.role: Front throat sheet shows the transition from the round boiler barrel into the squared firebox wrapper.

parts.name: Exposed Firebox Backhead
parts.role: Rear firebox plate is exposed at the cab front to show where controls and firing gear meet the boiler.

parts.name: Crew Cab with Cutaway Side
parts.role: Crew cab is narrowed on the port side so the turbine and gearbox below remain visible in the ISO view.

parts.name: Cab Roof
parts.role: Thin cab roof caps the crew compartment without hiding the under-cab machinery.

parts.name: Cab Floor Plate
parts.role: Thin floor plate supports the crew area and leaves the turbine train legible below it.

parts.name: Brass Locomotive Bell
parts.role: Bell on top of the smokebox provides the audible warning device.

parts.name: Quadruple Exhaust Stack A
parts.role: One of four separate exhaust tubes that create the S2's distinctive quadruple stack silhouette.

parts.name: Quadruple Exhaust Stack B
parts.role: Second exhaust tube, separated so the four-stack arrangement is visible rather than a single cylinder.

parts.name: Quadruple Exhaust Stack C
parts.role: Third exhaust tube channels smokebox draft upward from the turbine locomotive's long boiler.

parts.name: Quadruple Exhaust Stack D
parts.role: Fourth exhaust tube completes the signature PRR S2 exhaust cluster.

parts.name: Steam Dome
parts.role: Dome collects dry steam above the boiler waterline before steam is routed to appliances and turbine piping.

parts.name: Worthington Feedwater Heater
parts.role: Long Worthington heater preheats feedwater with exhaust steam before it enters the boiler.

parts.name: Port Feedwater Pump
parts.role: Pump below the running board moves heated feedwater from the tender supply into the boiler.

parts.name: Feedwater Return Pipe
parts.role: Visible pipe links the heater outlet back into the boiler shell.

parts.name: Port Elephant-Ear Smoke Deflector
parts.role: Large vertical port plate lifts smoke over the long boiler and makes the post-1946 S2 silhouette recognizable.

parts.name: Starboard Elephant-Ear Smoke Deflector
parts.role: Matching starboard deflector balances the smokebox and shows the paired Altoona modification.

parts.name: Port Deflector Front Stay
parts.role: Front stay braces the port smoke deflector to the smokebox shell.

parts.name: Port Deflector Rear Stay
parts.role: Rear stay prevents the port deflector plate from vibrating at speed.

parts.name: Starboard Deflector Front Stay
parts.role: Front stay braces the starboard smoke deflector to the smokebox shell.

parts.name: Starboard Deflector Rear Stay
parts.role: Rear stay prevents the starboard deflector plate from vibrating at speed.

parts.name: Port Deflector Top Edge Stiffener
parts.role: Top stiffener makes the port elephant-ear plate read as a braced sheet rather than a floating flat rectangle.

parts.name: Port Deflector Bottom Edge Stiffener
parts.role: Bottom stiffener ties the lower edge of the port deflector into the stay brackets.

parts.name: Port Deflector Diagonal Stay
parts.role: Diagonal stay triangulates the port deflector mount so the plate has a believable support path.

parts.name: Starboard Deflector Top Edge Stiffener
parts.role: Top stiffener makes the starboard elephant-ear plate read as a braced sheet.

parts.name: Starboard Deflector Bottom Edge Stiffener
parts.role: Bottom stiffener ties the starboard deflector into its stay brackets.

parts.name: Starboard Deflector Diagonal Stay
parts.role: Diagonal stay triangulates the starboard deflector mount so the plate is not visually unsupported.

parts.name: Port Running Board
parts.role: Port walkway gives maintenance access along the boiler and supports exposed pumps.

parts.name: Starboard Running Board
parts.role: Starboard walkway mirrors the port board and establishes the full boiler width.

parts.name: Port Twin Air Pump
parts.role: Port air pump supplies compressed air for train brakes from below the running board.

parts.name: Starboard Twin Air Pump
parts.role: Starboard air pump completes the paired brake-air equipment installation.

parts.name: Westinghouse Ahead Turbine
parts.role: Main ahead steam turbine sits exposed under the cab and delivers forward running power to the gearbox.

parts.name: Smaller Reverse Turbine
parts.role: Smaller reverse turbine provides backing movement without separate reciprocating cylinders.

parts.name: Steam Delivery Pipe to Turbine
parts.role: Large external pipe carries boiler steam rearward to the turbine housing so the power path is visible.

parts.name: Reduction Transmission Gearbox
parts.role: Gearbox reduces turbine speed and sends torque to the fourth driving axle.

parts.name: Drive Shaft to Geared Axle
